Pinned 4.2.2 source parser evaluates to 40202; Lean Nat literal and Rocq N result checked by reduction. Representation differs, value agrees.
Flocq simple alias resolves to Corelib.SpecFloat.cond_Zopp. Same Boolean sign branch and unrestricted integer domain; paired typed law, runtime boundary cases and differential oracle.

Imported Corelib.SpecFloat.iter_pos has direct binary-positive recursion. Lean body now follows its three constructors, with a closed universal theorem preserving the previous natural-iteration semantics. Paired execution and independent affine closed-form oracle.
Same unrestricted integer arguments and implication from -y <= -x to x <= y. Closed exact-typed clients in both assistants.
Same unrestricted integer arguments and implication from y < x to x != y. Closed exact-typed clients in both assistants.

Coq-generated equality eliminator is used locally to establish Boolean equality-proof irrelevance. Lean uses built-in proof irrelevance via Subsingleton.elim; no numeric algorithm or artificial same-named API is required. Not a literal port of the generated eliminator.

Same dependent true branch compares data/proofs with the distinguished element; false branch is False. Lean permits Sort u, extending the source Type-indexed interface; paired branch equations check the source specialization.
Same universal equality of two proofs of b=true. Lean uses Subsingleton.elim rather than the source-generated equality eliminator; exact theorem type preserved.

Same unrestricted integer parity decomposition. Source Z.even is represented by decidable Lean Even; the paired client checks the Boolean conditional specialization, including negative inputs through the universal theorem.

Same unrestricted integer base and two nonnegative exponent premises, with multiplication on the right. Integer-power body is reviewed separately and fingerprinted here; weakening either exponent domain is not silently accepted.
Same nonnegative exponent premise. Source Z.abs_nat corresponds to Int.natAbs; negative integer powers are zero and are not absolute-exponent powers.
Same natural-exponent successor equation and unrestricted signed integer base. Lean uses ordinary Nat-indexed integer power for the source Zpower_nat.
Same positive base premise and genuine binary-positive exponent domain. Lean Zpower_pos uses its positiveToNat transport; paired typed clients check the source contract.
Same nonnegative exponent and odd-base Boolean hypotheses. Source Z.even is transported to decidable Even; the result refers to actual integer Zpower, not an absolute-exponent substitute.

Source record has an integer field with Boolean proof Z.leb 2 value = true. Lean Radix has the same integer domain with proposition proof 2 <= value. Paired clients bridge both proof presentations; Lean projections are explicit rather than source coercions. Constructor and field types are fingerprinted, not only the empty record-type hash.

Same unrestricted integer projection from an admissible radix record. The carrier's proposition-versus-Boolean proof adaptation is recorded at radix; Lean uses explicit .val where the source coerces a radix to Z.

Same at-least-two admissibility condition, expressed as a Lean proposition instead of source Z.leb Boolean equality. Both conversions are checked in paired clients; radix zero/one are not newly admitted.
Same implication from equal integer projections to equal records. Lean proof irrelevance replaces the source Boolean-equality helper without weakening admissibility.
Same radix value two and a checked proof of admissibility; paired definitional-equality clients.
Same positivity statement for every valid radix; explicit Lean .val replaces the source coercion.
Same strict lower bound one for every valid radix; explicit Lean .val replaces the source coercion.
Same valid radix and strictly positive integer-exponent premise; conclusion is strictly greater than one.
Same valid radix and nonnegative integer-exponent premise; zero exponent is allowed, negative exponents are not.
Same valid radix and all-integer exponent quantification. The negative-exponent branch is zero, so no extra nonnegativity premise is introduced.
Same valid radix and exponent-order hypothesis over all integers. Both negative powers may be zero; non-strict monotonicity still holds.

Same valid radix, nonnegative UPPER exponent and strict exponent order. Lower exponent may be negative. Both assistants prove that removing the upper-exponent premise is false using -2 < -1 but zero equal powers.

Same all-integer exponent implication from power(e1-1) < power(e2) to e1 <= e2. The reviewed direct theorem uses Zpower; the unused former check/spec wrapper had an unrelated natAbs premise and has been removed.
Same unrestricted integer index and valid radix. Negative indices are below the zero negative-power result; no natAbs exponent is substituted.

Same signed dividend, positive a and nonnegative b premises. Source floor modulo agrees with Lean Euclidean modulo on the resulting nonnegative divisor domain, including zero; paired clients and universal Lean floor/Euclidean bridges preserve that boundary.
Same unconditional quotient/remainder decomposition over all signed integers, including divisor zero. Source Z.quot/Z.rem are Lean Int.tdiv/Int.tmod, not default division/modulo.
Same unconditional nested truncating-remainder identity for all signed n,a,b, including zero factors. No spurious nonzero-divisor assumption.

Same arbitrary dividend and two nonnegative factor premises. Source floor division/modulo matches Lean Euclidean operations on these premises; zero cases retained, negative-divisor global alias explicitly rejected.
Same unconditional truncating nested-remainder/division identity for signed and zero inputs. Actual operations are tmod/tdiv, with no added positivity conditions.
Same strict |a| < b premise and zero truncated quotient. Lean spells |a| as integer-cast natAbs; the paired Lean client uses absolute value and checks their equivalence without extra premises.
Same strict |a| < b premise and remainder equal to a, with the same natAbs/absolute-value presentation bridge as the quotient law.

Same all-signed inputs, genuine 0 <= a*b hypothesis and unrestricted divisor including zero. Conclusion uses truncating quotients/remainders. Both assistants prove that the premise-free claim is false at a=-2,b=1,c=2; obsolete Euclidean check wrapper was removed.
